observationsNotFindings: The redraft took the remedy I preferred rather than the cheaper one. I offered two paths: issue a re-measured successor and record it, or keep recording v4 with the historical scoping disclosed. It did the first and folded the second in anyway, so the entry both records a currently-measured artifact and states plainly what v4 was and why it is not that artifact. The second path alone would have satisfied the finding; doing both leaves less for a later reader to reconstruct.

Turn 2 pins the turn-1 record into itself — the frozen turn-1 subject and both turn-1 verdicts appear in measured inputs with digests that recompute. That is what let me check the disposition against my own frozen text rather than against the draft's paraphrase of it, and it is worth noting as a property of the turn-2 form rather than of this entry specifically.

'Does not unwrite the turn-1 OBJECT' is a small sentence doing real work. A turn-2 redraft that answered an objection could quietly present itself as the only draft; this one keeps the objection in the record alongside its disposition.

'Wave 2' now appears in three consecutive entries — D-171, D-172 turn 1 and D-172 turn 2 — with still no referent anywhere in live COORD. I have declined it each time on the same grounds and will keep doing so, but a term appearing in three adopted-track entries without a definition is drifting toward being load-bearing by repetition. It wants either a definition in COORD or removal before adoption; that is a call for you, not a defect I can charge.

One thing I did not do: revisit whether my turn-1 MUST-FIX was correctly severity-graded. Codex returned CONSENT 0/0 on the same draft, so the two lanes disagreed about whether recording v4 was blocking. I have not read that verdict and take no view on it; the disagreement is the coordinator's to resolve, and it is resolved in practice here since the redraft satisfies both lanes.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No MUST-FIX, no SHOULD-FIX. CLAUDE-D172-MF1 is landed by the remedy I named first and preferred, with the alternative folded in as well: the entry now records exact-bytes-leftover-join.v5 rather than v4, and it states plainly what v4 was and why it is not the artifact being recorded. I verified the remedy in v5's own bytes rather than through the draft — head, recordedInputs.HEAD, file08Pin and both requiredNowUnchanged fields all equal live by ==, which is precisely the claim the draft's live-remeasurement paragraph makes. Every surviving 26 and 5d5d778 in the draft is explicitly historical and paired with the live value in the same sentence, where turn 1 contained no occurrence of either. All eleven cited digests recompute, including three the turn-1 entry did not carry — the frozen turn-1 subject and both turn-1 verdicts — which is what let me check the disposition against my own frozen verdict rather than the draft's paraphrase: it reports my verdict as OBJECT with 1 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, which is exact, and restates the finding without softening it. Every live figure matches the register, D-172 remains the next unused heading, and 'Does not unwrite the turn-1 OBJECT' keeps the objection in the record alongside its disposition. Two things for you rather than as defects. 'Wave 2' now appears in three consecutive entries with no referent in COORD; I have declined it each time but repetition is making it look load-bearing. And Codex returned CONSENT 0/0 at turn 1 on the draft I objected to — I have not read that verdict and take no view on the disagreement, which this redraft resolves in practice by satisfying both lanes.
